why:
RFC-0043's component seam for timers, and the most-written member of the family: every C++ example workspace and the `nros new` scaffold contains `::nros::bind_timer<Talker, &Talker::on_tick>(node, timer_, 500, this)`. It binds a component MEMBER `void C::tick()` as the timer callback by identity, with a compile-time trampoline and the component pointer as `ctx`, writing the timer into caller-owned storage. rclcpp's `create_wall_timer(period, std::bind(&Talker::on_tick, this))` allocates a `std::function`; there is no allocator here. See `cpp:bind_subscription` for the family and `cpp:ComponentNode::create_timer` for the RFC-0044 tier that wraps it.
